header: Gold and silver in India (IBJA rates and their trend). I read nothing from the caller; I ask the IBJA page, read it with src/lib/live/gold.ts, and answer with the source and the time. The trend is IBJA's own record (about four months), lengthened to a year with ESTIMATED days from the NSE gold/silver ETFs when those can be had (always marked as estimates). If the page cannot be reached I return the last good answer, marked stale; if the page has changed so that the numbers cannot be found, it is an error, never a guess.

symbols.name: etfUrl
doc: For the year before IBJA's page begins I use the NSE-traded gold and silver ETFs (see the end of src/lib/live/gold.ts). Fixed addresses, asked at most once in six hours. I ask from a week BEFORE the date one year back (so that the day of that date, or the trading day before it, is in the record) to now

symbols.name: savedRecords
symbols.sig: function savedRecords(): { gold: EtfSeries; silver: EtfSeries; savedThrough: string } | null
symbols.returns: { gold: EtfSeries; silver: EtfSeries; savedThrough: string } | null
doc: This is the copy of the two records kept with the app: past prices do not change, so I serve it whenever the live source does not answer

symbols.name: etfRecords
symbols.sig: async function etfRecords(): Promise<{ gold: EtfSeries; silver: EtfSeries; savedThrough?: string } | { why: string }>
symbols.returns: Promise<{ gold: EtfSeries; silver: EtfSeries; savedThrough?: string } | { why: string }>
doc: Returns the two ETF records (live, else the saved copy), or why neither could be had (the chart then stays on IBJA's own days). It never throws.

symbols.name: savedAnswers
doc: Returns the saved last good answer, or none when the database cannot be had: I do not let the card fail because of it
